channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: Laopu Gold's profit rose 88.18%, and the interim dividend took 74.6% of it
item.description: The Hong Kong-listed jeweller reported 19.81 billion yuan of revenue for the first half, up 60.3%, and 4.267 billion yuan of profit, up 88.18%. It will pay out 18.02 yuan a share.

item.title: Movado's sales rose 4.9%, the exact figure by which Fossil's fell
item.description: The quarter to 31 July put Movado's net sales at $169.8 million and net income at $12.3 million against $3.0 million a year earlier, helped by $3.2 million of tariff duty refunds.

item.title: Delhi's customs chief heard eight grievances in Mumbai and asked for a chart
item.description: The Finance Minister nominated Manish Kumar to meet the trade at GJEPC's head office on 24 August. Rough valuation, 100% checking at Mumbai and misdeclaration proceedings led the list.

item.title: Ten Chinese gold counters priced within seven yuan of each other
item.description: On 25 August the brand boards read 1,403 to 1,410 yuan a gram, a spread of 0.499%. Chow Sang Sang added 18 yuan in a session, Chow Tai Fook 17.

item.title: Platinum's held mark broke after seven sessions, and gold gave up $42.80
item.description: The carried platinum figure of $1,881.00 sat $19.00 above the entire day range, so this desk rewrote the tape to $1,816.00. Gold fell 0.926% and silver 0.721%.

item.title: $457,700 led Doyle, and an 1890 sapphire pair beat its estimate by 180%
item.description: A 12.46-carat D VS2 ring took Doyle's Important Jewelry sale at $457,700, 30.8% above its high estimate. Four of the top five lots cleared the book, and the widest margin was a pair of sapphire earrings.

item.title: A royal brooch made 23,750 pounds at Elmwood's; a 1927 feather made 75,000
item.description: The Verdura unicorn brooch from Queen Elizabeth II's lady-in-waiting drew the coverage at Elmwood's 19 August sale. Three other lots sold for more, and a Van Cleef feather brooch made 3.16 times as much.

item.title: Kagem brings rough emeralds to Jaipur, and 60 cutters skip the London room
item.description: The 13th India Rough Gemstones Sourcing Show opened on 24 August and runs to 11 September. Zambia's Kagem is showing rough emeralds to more than 60 Indian manufacturers who would otherwise bid in London.

item.title: Fossil's sales fell 4.9%, and watches were the line that held
item.description: Fossil's quarter to 4 July shows net sales down 4.9% to $209.7 million. Traditional watches fell 1.5%, leathers fell 31.1% and jewellery fell 11.2%. Across six months, traditional watch sales rose.

item.title: Four tests on one rough stone, and only the last one settled it
item.description: The Israeli Diamond Institute reports a rough diamond that passed visual screening as natural, drew a qualified flag from a CVD detector, and was classified Type IIa by infrared. Single-source, and no weight published.

item.title: Gold gives back $21.60 in two sessions while silver takes back 0.99%
item.description: Gold was written back at $4,622.30 this morning, down $11.90 on yesterday's mark and $21.60 below Monday's. Silver went the other way at $68.55. Platinum and palladium held a sixth session.

item.title: 1,004.21 in Shanghai, and five bank counters spread 16.60 yuan apart
item.description: Shanghai's Au99.99 closed at 1,004.21 yuan a gram, up 2.10%, back above a level it has broken both ways before. Five bank savings-gold counters quoted between 1,005.69 and 1,022.29 the same morning.

item.title: $594 million from China, and a prototype press at IIT Madras
item.description: India imported about $594 million of rough lab-grown diamonds from China and Hong Kong in FY2025-26. A 242 crore rupee programme at IIT Madras has now run a prototype HPHT press. Single source.

item.title: $1,195 million to $307 million: Surat shrugs at Russia's cutting cluster
item.description: India's rough imports from Russia fell from $1,195 million in FY2022-23 to $307 million in FY2025-26, a fall of 74.3%. Surat's manufacturers say a Yakutia cluster changes nothing.

item.title: 560 applicants for 27 places: the watch trade's arithmetic problem
item.description: Rolex's Dallas school took 27 of more than 560 applicants in 2024. North Seattle College takes 10 to 12 a year. America had about 6,500 watchmakers in 2021, against 44,000 in 1953.

item.title: 39 of 48 lots away in Sydney, and the diamond still waits
item.description: Bonhams' Fine Jewellery sale opened in Sydney at 18:00 AEST with 135 lots. At New York press time 39 of the first 48 had sold. The AU$120,000 to AU$180,000 diamond had not been reached.

item.title: Gübelin sprays synthetic DNA onto melee, and rough still defeats it
item.description: Provenance Proof, Gübelin's subsidiary, is marking polished melee from KGK Suisse with synthetic-DNA nanoparticles carrying mine, period and country. Rough defeats it: deep boiling strips the coating.

item.title: $4,643.90: gold sets the highest mark this tape has carried
item.description: Gold was written back to the tape at $4,643.90 an ounce, up $41.50 or 0.90% on Friday's print and $485.60 above this tape's 5 August mark. Silver eased to $68.74.

item.title: Gem Diamonds' half-year averages $1,395 a carat, up 38%
item.description: The Letšeng producer sold 42,624 carats for $59.5 million in the first half, averaging $1,395 against $1,008 a year earlier. Eight stones cleared $1 million each, for $16.1 million.

item.title: $374 million to Australia: India's jewellery exports there rose 16%
item.description: India's gem and jewellery exports to Australia reached $374 million in FY2025-26, up 16%. Gold jewellery rose more than 28%, silver nearly 30%, coloured stones almost 36%.

item.title: Doha signs Singapore, Shanghai and Tokyo, and says so 33 days later
item.description: The Qatar Diamond Exchange signed cooperation agreements with the Singapore, Shanghai and Tokyo bourses at a congress that closed 15 July, and announced them on 17 August.

item.title: 999.46 in Shanghai: three counters priced the same night three different ways
item.description: Shanghai's Au(T+D) closed 0.54 yuan short of 1,000 a gram, up 2.06%. Lao Miao added 2.51% at the counter, Chow Sang Sang 1.61%. The Saturday price tables carry Friday's board.

item.title: Israel's rough trade fell 35%, its polished 18%: the leading leg fell hardest
item.description: First-half figures give the categorical split this paper has carried only in aggregate: polished exports $625.7m, down 22.3%; rough exports $191.2m, down 34.6%. The rough legs together fell 35.3% against 18.1%.

item.title: Gold breaks $4,550 in Beijing and adds $47.96 more by New York
item.description: Eastmoney timestamped spot gold at $4,554.44 on Friday's Beijing afternoon. This paper's tape carries Friday's last New York print at $4,602.40, up $20.80. Same session, ten hours apart, and both are printed.

item.title: India's July gold imports more than double to $4.16 billion
item.description: The World Gold Council puts July imports at $4.16 billion against $1.97 billion in June, with volumes at 40 to 45 tonnes against 20. The ETF leg went the other way, down 55% on the month.

item.title: One Chinese refiner in, two out: the LBMA's seventeen days
item.description: Shenzhen Zhonghenglong joined the gold Good Delivery List on 17 August. Shandong Gold Smelting came off both lists on 5 August, and Hunan Shuikoushan off the silver list on 21 August. All three are Chinese.

item.title: Yoram Dvash takes the chair at the company that sells 30% of Debswana
item.description: Botswana's state rough trader has named the former World Federation of Diamond Bourses president as board chairman, two months after his term there ended. The seat he replaced had been empty since November.

item.title: Vasant Mehta, who chaired GJEPC through the crash years, dies at 81
item.description: He was the council's vice chairman in 1991-92 and again in 2006-08, chairman from 2008 to 2010, and convenor of its banking, insurance and taxation committee for years after that.

item.title: Miniso grows 53% and takes the top of NRF's Hot 25
item.description: Kantar ranks the fastest-growing US retailers on domestic sales growth from 2024 to 2025. Dick's Sporting Goods is second at 49% after buying Foot Locker, and every name in the top five is a value format.

item.title: Platinum adds 4.56% and takes the tape's biggest move from gold
item.description: Kitco read gold $4,581.60, silver $69.31, platinum $1,881.00 and palladium $1,336.00 at 05:59 New York. All four are written back, and platinum and palladium come off a one-session hold.
